title: observability: token-level KV metrics + cost/latency dashboard + alert tuning
author: Lena Chen
description:
Summary: Add token-level KV cache metrics, token-level cost/latency breakdowns (per-route + per-model), Grafana dashboard JSON, and tuned Prometheus alert rules for token-latency and KV cache regressions. This PR unblocks the next phase of cost-focused SLOs and provides clearer triage signals for latency regressions that correlate to KV cache hit/miss rates.

Motivation:
- Operators and SREs need visibility into per-token cost and latency (not just p50/p95 request-level) to attribute cost to long generations and to detect inefficient KV cache behavior.
- Current alerts are noisy during short bursts where batching changes latency but not cost; adding token-level signals reduces false positives and shortens MTTR.

What changed:
- metrics: export token-level counters and histograms (token_generation_count, token_generation_latency_seconds, kv_cache_hit_count, kv_cache_miss_count, kv_cache_latency_seconds) with labels {model, route, customer_tier, shard}.
- tracing: add span annotations for KV cache hit/miss and token emit events to link traces to metrics.
- dashboards: new Grafana dashboard JSON (dashboards/grafana/token_kv_cost_latency.json) with panels for token cost breakdown, KV hit-rate heatmap, per-model token latency histogram, and end-to-end trace links.
- alerts: tuned Prometheus rules to use token-level rate and error ratios; added composite alerting to suppress request-level alerts when token-level indicators are healthy.
- docs: updated docs/observability/token_metrics.md with metric naming, dashboards, and runbook guidance.

Testing:
- Unit tests for metric registration and labels added.
- Integration test in perf-canary environment validated metrics emission and dashboard panels.
- Alert rules tested against synthetic trace/metric generator in staging.

Rollback plan:
- Alerts can be toggled via the SRE dashboard. Metric names are additive and safe; dashboards/alerts can be rolled back by reverting the config map.

Notes:
- This PR intentionally keeps metric cardinality bounded by limiting customer_tier and route labels to enums and by sampling long-tail routes.
- Follow-up work: add cost attribution per-tenant (ENG-4601) and refine sampling for very high-cardinality workloads.

Checklist:
- [x] Add metrics and histograms
- [x] Update tracing spans
- [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON
- [x] Add Prometheus alert rules and silence logic
- [x] Update docs and runbook
- [x] Integration tests in canary
